items.title: Early NBA Minimum Salary Projections For 2027/28
items.content:
The NBA’s minimum salary is one of several figures that changes from year to year at the same rate as the league’s salary cap. If the cap increases by 5% from one season to the next, the minimum salary will rise by the same amount.

That means that even though we don’t know yet exactly where the minimum salaries will end up for the 2027/28 season, we can make an educated estimate. The NBA’s most recent projection for ’27/28 called for a $174MM cap, which is the figure we’ll use to project next season’s minimum salaries.

[RELATED: NBA Minimum Salaries For 2026/27]

A player’s minimum salary is determined in part by how much NBA experience he has — a veteran who has 10+ seasons under his belt is eligible for a significantly higher minimum salary than a rookie would be.

Based on the current 2027/28 cap estimate, next year’s rookie minimum salary will exceed $1.4MM, while the minimum for a veteran with 10+ years of service will rise north of $4MM for the first time.

It’s worth noting that these figures will only apply to players who sign new minimum-salary contracts in 2027/28. The ’27/28 salaries for players with multiyear minimum deals will look a little different. For example, a rookie who signed a two-year deal worth the minimum ahead of the 2026/27 season would have a second-year salary of $2,294,370 for ’27/28, as we outline here.

We’ll update these projections later in the season if the NBA adjusts its cap estimate for the 2027/28 season, and then again next year when the league officially sets the ’27/28 cap.
